description: Cross-examine guide: benchmark pricing ratios and commitment optimization tips for cross-cloud what-if analysis. Ratios represent typical relative cost for equivalent services (1.0 = same cost, <1.0 = cheaper, >1.0 = more expensive). These are industry averages — actual costs depend on negotiated rates.

compute_vm.notes: GCP SUDs (sustained use discounts) make GCP cheapest for steady VMs. AWS has best spot market depth.

compute_vm_general_purpose.description: General-purpose VMs: Azure D/Ds/Dv-series ↔ AWS m-series ↔ GCP n2-standard/c3-standard
compute_vm_general_purpose.notes: General-purpose workloads. Azure D-series maps to AWS m5/m6i/m7i. AWS typically 5-10% cheaper on-demand.

compute_vm_compute_optimized.description: Compute-optimized VMs: Azure F/Fs-series ↔ AWS c-series ↔ GCP c3-highcpu/c2
compute_vm_compute_optimized.notes: Compute-heavy workloads. AWS c-series has strongest price/performance. Azure F-series ~14% more expensive on-demand.

compute_vm_memory_optimized.description: Memory-optimized VMs: Azure E/Es-series ↔ AWS r-series ↔ GCP n2-highmem/c3-highmem
compute_vm_memory_optimized.notes: Memory-intensive workloads (databases, caches). AWS r-series ~11% cheaper than Azure E-series on-demand.

compute_vm_storage_optimized.description: Storage-optimized VMs: Azure L-series ↔ AWS i/d-series ↔ GCP n2-standard (local SSD)
compute_vm_storage_optimized.notes: Storage-heavy workloads (big data, NoSQL). Local NVMe performance and pricing vary significantly.

compute_vm_gpu.description: GPU VMs: Azure N-series ↔ AWS p/g-series ↔ GCP a2/g2
compute_vm_gpu.notes: GPU pricing depends heavily on GPU model (A100 vs T4 vs V100). AWS has widest GPU instance selection.

compute_vm_burstable.description: Burstable VMs: Azure B-series ↔ AWS t-series ↔ GCP e2/f1-micro
compute_vm_burstable.notes: Burstable instances for dev/test and low-utilization workloads. GCP e2 shared-core is cheapest for light workloads.

compute_serverless.notes: Pricing highly depends on invocation count vs. duration vs. memory. AWS Lambda has best cold-start performance.

compute_containers.notes: Cloud Run is often cheapest for bursty container workloads due to per-request billing.

kubernetes.notes: AKS has no control plane fee. GKE Autopilot simplifies cost management. EKS charges $0.10/hr per cluster.

storage_object.notes: Egress costs vary significantly. GCS has cheapest storage; AWS S3 has most tiering options.

storage_block.notes: Performance tiers and IOPS pricing differ significantly across clouds.

database_relational.notes: Azure SQL has good price/performance for SQL Server workloads (no license cost). RDS has broadest engine support.

database_nosql.notes: Cosmos DB tends to be most expensive but offers multi-model and global distribution. DynamoDB on-demand is simple but can be costly at scale.

data_warehouse.notes: BigQuery serverless model is cheapest for ad-hoc queries. Redshift reserved nodes best for steady workloads.

networking_cdn.notes: CDN pricing depends heavily on traffic volume and origin location.

monitoring.notes: GCP Cloud Monitoring has generous free tier. CloudWatch custom metrics can be expensive.

messaging.notes: SQS is cheapest for simple queuing. Pub/Sub best for high-throughput streaming.

ml_platform.notes: GPU pricing varies significantly by instance type. GCP has best TPU options for training.

cache.notes: Pricing is similar across clouds for Redis. ElastiCache Serverless adds flexibility but at higher per-request cost.

aws.action: Consider AWS Savings Plans (Compute or EC2) or Reserved Instances

azure.action: Consider Azure Reserved VM Instances or Azure Savings Plan
options: Azure Hybrid Benefit for Windows/SQL (~40% additional)

gcp.action: Consider GCP Committed Use Discounts (CUDs) — SUDs already auto-apply

migration_considerations.data_transfer: Egress costs are typically $0.08-0.12/GB. Factor in one-time migration data transfer costs.
migration_considerations.feature_parity: Not all services are 1:1 equivalent. Validate feature requirements before switching.
migration_considerations.lock_in: Consider API compatibility, proprietary features, and ecosystem dependencies.
migration_considerations.downtime: Plan for migration downtime or parallel-run costs during transition.
migration_considerations.compliance: Verify data residency and compliance requirements are met on target cloud.
